cards.text: About eight days after Jesus tells His disciples He must suffer, be killed and be raised to life (Luke 9:22), He takes three of them with Him: Peter, John and James. Out of the whole group, only THREE get the invite. Friend, the last time I got picked out of a group, I was in a clearance bin with a 25 cent sticker on my face.

cards.question: Jesus takes Peter, John and James up on a mountain. What does He go up there to do?

cards.text: So up on the mountain, Jesus prays. And as He's praying, the appearance of His face changes, and His clothes become radiantly white.

Then, SUDDENLY, two men are there talking with Jesus: Moses, who led Israel long ago, and Elijah, the prophet. Friend, if two people showed up in my bakery out of nowhere, I'd be face first in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Moses and Elijah are talking with Jesus on the mountain. What do they talk about?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Peter and his companions are overcome by sleep, with Moses and Elijah RIGHT THERE. Friend, I can't judge, because I lay in a junk drawer for YEARS without doing a single thing.

cards.question: True or false: by the time Peter and his companions wake up, Moses and Elijah are already gone.
When Peter and his companions wake up, they see Jesus' ___ and the two men standing with Him.

cards.text: As Moses and Elijah are leaving, Peter speaks up: “Master, it is good for us to be here.” I think Peter wants this moment to last, friend.

cards.question: Peter wants to put up three ___ on the mountain: one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah.
Right after Peter's idea about the shelters, Luke adds a short note about Peter. What does it say?

answers.text: He did not know what he was saying
He was speaking for all three of them
He had been planning it for days

cards.text: Peter isn't even done talking when a cloud appears and wraps all around them. I know that feeling, friend: the oven timer goes off every time I start a good story.

cards.question: True or false: the disciples are afraid as they enter the cloud.

cards.text: Then a voice comes from the cloud. Friend, when a voice speaks out of a cloud, even I stop talking.

cards.question: The voice from the cloud says Jesus is His ___, whom He has chosen.
True or false: the voice from the cloud tells the disciples to listen to Moses and Elijah.

cards.text: After the voice has spoken, the disciples look around the mountain.

cards.question: After the voice from the cloud has spoken, who is still there with the disciples?
True or false: in those days, the disciples tell everyone what they saw on the mountain.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the core action. The disciples are overcome by sleep during a glorious moment, but the comparison is Papa Dorin lying in a junk drawer doing nothing. Being idle in a drawer for years isn't the same action as falling asleep while something amazing happens, so the line doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "I lay in a junk drawer for YEARS without doing a single thing" contradicts his backstory. After the can opener arrived, he welcomed and calmed every newcomer, and the drawer held rubber band contests and other ways to pass the time.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This is the central moment of the passage, Jesus' face changing and His clothes becoming radiantly white, but the card is a flat restatement of the verse with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice or reaction.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a bare transition ("the disciples look around the mountain") with no Papa Dorin voice. It only exists to set up card 18.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The voice's command, "Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35), is the climax of the passage, but the walkthrough only touches it as a false statement ("listen to Moses and Elijah"). No story card or choice card ever tells the baker, positively, who they are told to listen to.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
